A_target.statement:
Let $\PP$ be a set of [[Definition:Partial Recursive Function|partial computable functions]] with $\PP \ne \O$ and $\PP$ not the set of all of them.
Then $\set {e: \phi_e \in \PP}$ is not [[Definition:Decidable Set|decidable]].

B_source.statement: The [[Definition:Halting Problem|halting problem]] $\set {\tuple {p, x}: p \text { halts on } x}$ is not decidable.

substitutions.halting of p on x: membership of a constructed program q in the property P

object_map.reformulation: Reduce halting to the property by building a program that behaves like a fixed member of P exactly when p halts on x.

validity_conditions: Replacing P by its complement, one may assume the nowhere-defined function is not in P.
The construction of q from p and x is computable, by the s-m-n theorem.
proof_plan: Replacing $\PP$ by its complement if necessary, assume the nowhere-defined function is not in $\PP$, and fix $e_1$ with $\phi_{e_1} \in \PP$.
Given $\tuple {p, x}$, effectively construct a program $q$ which on input $y$ first runs $p$ on $x$ and, if that halts, outputs $\map {\phi_{e_1} } y$.
If $p$ halts on $x$ then $\phi_q = \phi_{e_1} \in \PP$; otherwise $\phi_q$ is nowhere defined, so $\phi_q \notin \PP$.
